title: Install an extension
summary: Find an extension in the Marketplace, install it and see where it lives.

steps.say: Click inside the VS Code window so it is in front.
hints: The title bar should end with Visual Studio Code.
Press Alt Tab to switch to it.
steps.why: The Extensions shortcut only reaches the window in front.

steps.say: Press Control Shift X to open the Extensions view.

checks.prompt: Is the Extensions view open in the side bar with a Search Extensions in Marketplace box?

hints: Extensions is the icon made of four squares in the Activity Bar.
Or open the View menu and choose Extensions.
steps.why: The Extensions view searches the Marketplace and manages what is installed.

steps.say: Type Code Spell Checker in the search box at the top of the Extensions view.

checks.prompt: Does the Extensions list show Code Spell Checker as a result?

hints: Check the publisher name and download count to pick the genuine extension.
Any extension you like is fine; spell checking is a harmless one to practice with.
steps.why: Searching by name finds extensions without leaving VS Code.

steps.say: Click the blue Install button next to Code Spell Checker.

checks.prompt: Has the Install button for Code Spell Checker changed to a gear icon or Uninstall, showing it is installed?

hints: Install sits on the right of the result, or at the top of its details page.
VS Code may ask whether you trust the publisher; read the name before agreeing.
steps.why: Installed extensions start working right away in every folder.

steps.say: Clear the search box. The Installed section now lists the new extension.

checks.prompt: Does an Installed section in the Extensions view list Code Spell Checker?

hints: Press Escape or delete the text to clear the box.
Right-click an installed extension to disable or uninstall it later.
steps.why: Knowing where extensions are listed lets you turn them off if one causes trouble.
